chapter.title: Asking the model to explain the change

cards.body:
Yesterday the agent found the changed lines. Now it hands them to the reader. **Give the reader only the clipping, not the whole newspaper.**

Picture the clipping service's desk: one cut-out strip, 4 lines long, and a sticky note that says 'What changed? 2 sentences. Quote the line.' Not a stack of 5 full papers with a vague 'anything interesting?'
cards.simpler: Yesterday the agent found the lines that changed. Today it passes them to the reader. **Give the reader only the clipping, not the whole newspaper.** Think of a clipping service. On the desk sits one cut-out strip, 4 lines long, with a sticky note: 'What changed? 2 sentences. Quote the line.' That beats a stack of 5 full papers and a vague 'anything interesting?'

cards.prompt: Your clipping-service reader gets two desks to pick from. Desk A: the full 40-page Monday paper and a note saying 'tell me about Quillpad.' Desk B: a 4-line strip cut from the pricing page and a note saying 'what changed, 2 sentences, quote the line.' Which desk gets you a note you can trust?

options.text: Desk A. More pages means a fuller answer.
Desk B. A small strip and a strict note.
Either. The reader is smart enough to cope with both.

whyNot.a: That's the whole newspaper, not the clipping: 40 pages gives the reader room to summarise things that never changed.
whyNot.c: That's hope, not a check: a reader with 40 pages and a vague note fills the gaps with guesses.

cards.reteach: The model is a fast reader, not a careful one. Hand it 4 changed lines and it has nowhere to wander. Hand it the whole page and it describes the page instead of the change.

cards.title: Less text, better answer
cards.body:
An AI model is a reader that writes back. Everything you send it is called the *prompt*: your instruction plus any text you want it to read. **The smaller the prompt, the less room the model has to drift.**

Yesterday's diff is already the smallest useful text: just the lines that are new or gone. Send those. Do not send the whole page, and never send both days' full copies and ask the model to find the difference itself. It will miss things, and it will invent things.

A diff of 6 lines costs almost nothing to send. A full pricing page is often 2,000 words of menus and footers.
cards.simpler: An AI model is a reader that writes back. What you send it is the prompt: your instruction plus the text to read. **The smaller the prompt, the less room the model has to drift.** Send only yesterday's diff, the lines that are new or gone. Never send the whole page, or both days' copies with 'find the difference'. It will miss things and invent things. A 6-line diff is cheap. A full page is often 2,000 words of menus and footers.

cards.title: Two lines in, two sentences out
cards.body:
Say your rival is a fictional note-taking app called Quillpad. Tuesday's diff of their pricing page is 2 lines. Gone: 'Pro plan: $8 per month'. New: 'Pro plan: $12 per month. Now includes offline sync.'

You send those 2 lines with the note: 'Say what changed in 2 sentences. Quote the exact line each claim comes from.'

The model writes back: 'Quillpad raised its Pro plan from $8 to $12 a month. The new line reads: Pro plan: $12 per month. Now includes offline sync.' Two sentences, one quote, **nothing you cannot check.**
cards.simpler: Quillpad is a made-up rival note app. Tuesday's pricing-page diff is 2 lines. Gone: 'Pro plan: $8 per month'. New: 'Pro plan: $12 per month. Now includes offline sync.' Send them with the note: 'What changed, in 2 sentences? Quote the line for each claim.' The model replies: 'Quillpad raised its Pro plan from $8 to $12 a month. The new line reads: Pro plan: $12 per month. Now includes offline sync.' Two sentences, one quote, **nothing you cannot check.**

cards.prompt: Wednesday the agent fetches Quillpad's changelog. The diff is 3 new lines about a dark mode release. What do you send the model?

options.text: The 3 new lines, plus the strict note.
Today's full changelog page, so the model has context.
Yesterday's and today's full pages, and ask the model to spot the difference.

whyNot.b: That's the whole newspaper, not the clipping: the model will happily summarise old entries that did not change.
whyNot.c: That's asking the model to do the diff's job: the comparison from chapter 4 already found the change exactly, with no guessing.

cards.reteach: The diff is the clipping. The model's only job is to put the clipping into plain words. Keep each tool to its job: the diff finds, the model explains.

cards.title: The strict note
cards.body:
The instruction has 3 parts, and each one closes a door. **Task, limit, source.**

*Task*: 'Say what changed.' Not 'summarise this', which invites a description of everything. *Limit*: '2 sentences.' A number, not 'briefly'. *Source*: 'Quote the exact line each claim comes from.' This is the part that lets you check the model's work in chapter 7.

Add one escape hatch: 'If nothing meaningful changed, say so.' Without it, the model will find something to say about a changed copyright year.
cards.simpler: The note has 3 parts. Each closes a door. **Task, limit, source.** The task is 'Say what changed.' Not 'summarise this', which invites a tour of everything. The limit is '2 sentences.' A number, not 'briefly'. The source is 'Quote the exact line each claim comes from.' That part lets you check its work in chapter 7. Add one escape hatch: 'If nothing meaningful changed, say so.' Without it, the model will comment on a changed copyright year.

cards.body: Priya built her agent in an evening and, to be safe, sent the model the full page every day with 'tell me anything important.' The summaries read well. On day 4 one said Quillpad had 'launched a new team plan.' The team plan had been on the page for a year. **The model described the page, not the change.** You spot this when a summary mentions something you cannot find in the diff.
cards.simpler: Priya built her agent in one evening. To be safe, she sent the model the full page every day with 'tell me anything important.' The summaries read well. On day 4 one said Quillpad had 'launched a new team plan.' The team plan had been on the page for a year. **The model described the page, not the change.** You spot this when a summary mentions something you cannot find in the diff.

cards.prompt: A friend asks why your prompt insists on 'quote the exact line.' Which answer is the one this chapter gave?

options.text: It makes the summary longer and more detailed.
It lets you check every claim against a real line, so an invented claim has nowhere to hide.
It helps the model find the change in the first place.

whyNot.a: That's the opposite of the point: the 2-sentence limit keeps it short, and the quote is there to be checked, not to pad.
whyNot.c: That's the diff's job, not the quote's: the comparison already found the change before the model saw anything.

cards.reteach: The quote is a receipt. The model says 'price went up' and hands you the line it read. If that line is not in the diff, the claim is made up, and you know in 10 seconds.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body: Send the model only the changed lines, never the whole page, so it has nothing to drift into. Give it a 3-part note, **what changed, 2 sentences, quote the line**, and every claim arrives with its receipt.
cards.simpler: Send the model only the lines that changed, never the whole page. Then it has nothing extra to wander into. Give it a 3-part note: **what changed, 2 sentences, quote the line.** Every claim then arrives with its receipt, like a shop receipt you can hold up against the diff and check.

cards.body: Open any AI chat you already use. Paste the 2 Quillpad lines from the example with the 3-part note. Then paste a whole pricing page with 'anything interesting?' and compare how much of each answer you could check.
cards.simpler: Open any AI chat you already use. Paste the 2 Quillpad lines from the example, along with the 3-part note. Read the answer. Then paste a whole pricing page and ask 'anything interesting?' **Compare how much of each answer you could check** against the text you gave it. Count the claims you can trace back to a line.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now write a 3-part prompt that turns a diff into a 2-sentence summary with a quoted source line.
